<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|36|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XIII.}}</noinclude>gathering vp the cockle, you may roote vp the vvheate also together vvith it. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=30}}† ‖ Suffer both to grovv vntil the haruest, and in the time of haruest I vvil say to the reapers, Gather vp first the cockle, and binde it into bundels to burne, but the vvheate gather ye into my barne.⊣

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=31}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 6 Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}An other parable he proposed vnto them, saying, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 4, 30. Luc. 13, 18.''}}* The kingdom of heauen is like to a mustard-seede, vvhich a man tooke and sovved in his field. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=32}}† Which is the ‖ least surely of al seedes: but vvhen it is grovven, it is greater then al herbes, and is made a tree, so that the foules of the aire come, and dvvel in the branches thereof. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=33}}† An other parable he spake to them, The kingdom of heauen is like to leauen, vvhich a vvoman tooke and hid in three measures of meale, vntil the vvhole vvas leauened.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=34}}† Al these things {{sc|Iesvs}} spake in parables to the multitudes, and vvithout parables he did not speake to them: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=35}}† that it might be fulfilled vvhich vvas spoken by the Prophet saying, I wil open my mouth in parables, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Psa. 77, 2.''}}* ''I wil vtter things hidden from the foundation of the vvorld''.⊣

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=36}}† Then hauing dimissed the multitudes, he came into the house, and his Disciples came vnto him, saying, Expound vs the parable of the cockle of the field. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=37}}† Who made ansvver and said to them, He that soweth the good seede, is the Sonne of man. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=38}}† And the field, is the vvorld. And the good seede: these are the childrē of the kingdom. And the cockle: are the children of the vvicked one. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=39}}† And the enemie that sovved them, is {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not God then, but the Diuel is the author of all euil.}}∷ the deuil. But the haruest, is the ende of the vvorld. And the reapers, are the Angels. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=40}}† Euen as cockle therfore is gathered vp, and burnt vvith fire: so shal it be in the ende of the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=41}}† The Sonne of man shal send his Angels, and they shal gather out of his kingdom al scandals, and them that vvorke iniquitie: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=42}}† and shal cast them into the furnace of fire, There shal be vveeping and gnashing of teeth. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=43}}† Then shal the iust shine as the sunne, in the kingdom of their father. He that hath eares to heare, let him heare.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=44}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for Virgins & other holy women.}}The kingdom of heauen is like a treasure hidden in a field. vvich a man hauing found, did hide it, and for ioy thereof goeth, and selleth al that he hath, and byeth that field. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=45}}† Againe the kingdom of heauen is like to a marchant man, seeking good pearles. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=46}}† And hauing found one precious pearle, he vvent his vvay, and sold al that he had, and<noinclude>{{rh|||bought}}</noinclude>
